object_description: stately three-storey solitaire with a permeable ground floor and a generous overhang
geometry_property: sectional ground floor extending into the basement
design_condition: the new volume takes the place of the old gymnasium in the middle of the axis between the two historic buildings, pushing the permissible boundary line and the proximity to them to the limit

positive: The new building secures the outdoor spaces necessary in the densely built-up district
The permeable ground floor and the generous overhang create exciting spatial impressions with the outdoor rooms
Shared access for parking and delivery is clever and pragmatic, preserving the turf field and circular track
The outdoor concept and the arrangement of break areas, hard pitches and grass fields agree with the urban concept
The open ground floor surprises with a sectional solution extending into the basement
It creates a flowing spatial relationship between entrance hall, lounge and the buried gymnasium
As a forum radiating in all directions the complex gains a captivating, identity-forming unique space
It offers a fruitful synergy with the future conversion of the existing gymnasium
A prefabricated concrete skeleton gives great flexibility in the spatial structure
Four powerful cross supports designed for a later increase form a clever structural starting point
Flexible 3.5 metre high room constellations open additional educational possibilities
The recognisable design desire for a workshop school enriches the traditional classrooms
The turn to the useful and practical gives the proposal a pleasant lightheartedness
The compact cluster of classrooms with studio character creates a diverse, community-promoting learning atmosphere
The facade structure is largely derived from the internal structure
The contribution impresses with structural clarity, flexible utility and high atmospheric qualities
The restrained architecture developed from structure and space complements the ensemble as a third contemporary witness
negative: The depth pushes the boundary line and proximity to the existing buildings to their limits
The spaces in between can hardly be perceived as pleasant access and lounge spaces
The unfavourable placement of the escape stairs exacerbates this
The support system consisting only of cross supports is exaggerated
The severely affected small spaces do not suggest continuing the structure into the lower basements
The winding access system with numerous narrow staircases makes orientation difficult
Whether the brittle solitaire can take on the connecting function between the historic buildings was controversial
The project exceeds the expected target costs
The ecological requirements can just about be achieved
